summary_html: Child achieves **permanency through legal guardianship** or kinship care. Federal programs provide funding parity with adoption for approved relatives.
authority_html:
- **Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act (FCSIAA)** — kinship-guardianship assistance  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. § 673(d))** — authorizes Guardianship Assistance Program (GAP)

primary_citations.citation_text: Hawaii — HRS Chapter 587A, Child Protective Act
Haw. Rev. Stat. §§ 346-391 and 346-395, Young Adult Voluntary Foster Care Program (purpose and age-twenty-one limit; eligibility)

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: In re Guardianship of I.W. and T.E.
key_cases.holding: The court held that the presumption that a fit parent acts in the child's best interest survives the parent's consent to a guardianship, and that article I, sections 5 and 6 of the Hawai'i Constitution require clear and convincing evidence of unfitness before that presumption may be set aside.
key_cases.relevance: This is the current Hawai'i standard governing guardianship as a permanency outcome: clear and convincing evidence of unfitness, with best interests judged by a preponderance.
key_cases.quote: the rebuttable presumption that a fit parent acts in the best interest of their child extends to guardianship proceedings

key_cases.holding: The court held that a hānai relative who is the child's resource caregiver has an interest sufficient to intervene as of right under HFCR Rule 24(a)(2) in a child welfare case, and that the family court must weigh the child's hānai relationships in the best-interests analysis.
key_cases.relevance: Permanency planning must account for hānai bonds, which can support guardianship or adoption by a non-blood kin caregiver.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that, when conducting a best interest of the child analysis, family courts must consider that child’s hānai relationships

key_cases.holding: The court held that DHS as permanent custodian has discretion in the first instance to select a child's permanent placement, that the party challenging the recommendation bears a preponderance burden, and that neither HRS chapter 587A nor Title IV-E imposes a mandatory relative-placement preference for permanent placement.
key_cases.relevance: Permanency through a relative or kin caregiver must be shown to be in the child's best interests by the challenging party, not presumed.
key_cases.quote: the party challenging DHS's permanent placement recommendation bears the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that the permanent placement is not in the child's best interests

key_cases.court: Intermediate Court of Appeals of Hawai'i
key_cases.holding: On competing adoption petitions for children in DHS permanent custody, the ICA held that family courts must separately determine whether the statutory consent requirement of HRS § 578-2 is met, and that the party contending DHS unreasonably withheld consent bears a preponderance burden.
key_cases.relevance: Foster or kin caregivers seeking permanency by adoption must carry the burden of showing DHS's refusal of consent was unreasonable.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the party challenging DHS's action bears the burden of proving, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the withholding of consent is unreasonable

key_cases.case_name: In re the Guardianship of Doe
key_cases.court: Intermediate Court of Appeals of Hawai'i
key_cases.holding: The ICA held that in deciding whether to terminate or continue a non-parent's guardianship of a minor the family court must consider the parental preference of HRS § 571-46(1) within the best-interests inquiry, adopting for Hawai'i a rebuttable custody presumption in favor of parents, but affirmed continuation of the grandparents' guardianship because the family court implicitly considered that preference and the evidence supported its order.
key_cases.relevance: It is the foundational Hawai'i decision treating guardianship as a permanency arrangement and fixing the weight the parental preference carries against a non-parent guardian.
key_cases.quote: we believe our jurisdiction is similar to the majority of jurisdictions which adopt a custody presumption in favor of parents subject to rebuttal

key_cases.case_name: In re the Guardianship of Doe
key_cases.court: Intermediate Court of Appeals of Hawai'i
key_cases.holding: The ICA held that the heightened clear and convincing standard of proof required to terminate parental rights does not apply to the parental-fitness question in a minor guardianship proceeding, because a guardianship of the person of a minor is neither absolute nor irrevocable, and it vacated the denial of the grandparents' co-guardianship petition and remanded for reconsideration.
key_cases.relevance: Anyone researching guardianship permanency in Hawai'i must know that this ICA decision's rejection of the heightened standard for parental fitness no longer states the law after In re Guardianship of I.W. and T.E.
key_cases.quote: We conclude the family court erred in applying a heightened standard of proof to the question of the fitness of the natural father.

state_agency.name: Hawaii Department of Human Services, Child Welfare Services
state_agency.hotline: 808-832-5300 (Oahu) or toll-free 1-888-380-3088 (Hawaii Island, Maui, Molokai, Lanai, Kauai), 24 hours a day, 7 days a week

extended_foster_care_age: 18 to 21 (voluntary Young Adult Voluntary Foster Care Program, "Imua Kakou"; qualifying path is department permanent, foster, voluntary foster, or court-ordered temporary foster custody at age eighteen, OR a guardianship entered after age sixteen whose legal guardians are no longer willing to provide emotional and financial support, OR an adoption after age sixteen whose adoptive parents are no longer willing to provide that support; plus consent, a court best-interest finding, and a school, work, or medical-condition criterion; HRS §§ 346-391, 346-395)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
